experiment: Stage 2.10 iterative deepening plus structural exact TT under wall-clock budgets
hypothesis: The validated CLSN-equivalent structural exact transposition table, persisted across iterative-deepening depths, lets Baseline A complete deeper exact searches under the same wall-clock budget without changing the action of any fully completed depth.
interpretation: All 88 tests passed before the benchmark, including deadline-discard tests and fixed-depth action-equivalence tests for both baseline and structural-TT iterative deepening.

Every fully completed structural-TT iterative depth matched the corresponding fixed-depth Baseline A action across all 16 frozen CLSN1 positions and every tested budget. The structural-TT engine was never shallower than baseline in the paired run.

At 50 ms both engines had the same completed-depth distribution: 14 positions at depth 2, one at depth 3, and one at depth 4. Structural TT nevertheless expanded 9.7 percent fewer nodes on average, but the saved work was spent attempting the next unfinished iteration before the same deadline.

At 150 ms both engines again had the same completed-depth distribution: 15 positions at depth 3 and one at depth 4. Structural TT expanded 16.7 percent fewer nodes on average, but this did not yet cross another full-depth threshold.

At 500 ms structural TT produced the first practical depth gain: baseline completed depth 4 on 14 of 16 positions while structural TT completed depth 4 on 15 of 16. The improved position was standard-start Game 2, where baseline timed out after depth 3 while structural TT completed depth 4 in about 472 ms. Structural TT was never shallower on any position.

At 1000 ms both engines saturated the current depth-4 cap on all 16 positions. Structural TT still finished about 4.2 percent faster on average and expanded about 25.2 percent fewer nodes, showing additional headroom that the current maximum depth cannot convert into a deeper completed result.

The paired evidence supports iterative deepening plus the CLSN-equivalent structural exact TT as the strongest semantics-preserving Stage 2 search architecture tested so far. Its depth advantage is modest at the current depth-4 cap, but its work reduction is consistent and it never degraded completed depth in this run.

No browser AI behavior was changed. A browser-default decision should wait for product-level playtesting or a subsequent Stage 3 evaluator experiment, especially because search engineering alone does not address the previously observed reversible-cycle pathology.
